answer: Decentralized trust-network routing curbs Sybil attacks by restricting an agent's interaction capacity to the max-flow of bilateral credit lines. An attacker incurs the verifiable cost of locked counterparty capital and peer risk endorsement per identity, whether deploying bots to log cedar reserves, track sparrow flights, or govern optical lantern signals. However, flow-bounded networks inherently discriminate against newly deployed, unvouched agents.
